authoredFrom: Input (built in tests/storage/producer-loss.test.ts from queue-count-overflow.json, seed et005b-queue-count-overflow): simulation.started at 10 ms (eventSeq 1); a job without cargo.loaded or market at 20 ms (2); 258 identical tolls of 5 at 30 ms (3-260); job.delivered at 250 ms (261) and the clear at 260 ms (262). No frame step, so no state is published (docs/simulator-v1.md, OD-5 S7): there are no snapshots, and both checkpoints show no job, so no late-attach trip can open (J9). Transport: a durable client at 0 ms that commits each item but whose ACKs are lost on the way (ack withhold), a disconnect at 100 ms, a durable client at 200 ms that commits and acknowledges each item, and a disconnect at 300 ms. One service.

Producer (protocol v1 §9, full store; queue-count-overflow.expected.json): with no ACK, an event is retained only while one entry stays free, so events 1-255 are retained and 256-260 are lost as queueCount. While connected each newly lost eventSeq is written as its own delta gap at its stream position, so connection 1 carries events 1-255 and the gaps [256], [257], [258], [259] and [260], each queueCount 1 with both lost times at the toll's occurrence (1,000,030,000,000 ns). Connection 2's checkpoint reports A = 0 and nextEventSeq 261; it redelivers 1-255 and the merged record [256, 260] (queueCount 5, redelivered), and the acknowledged store then admits 261 and 262 live.

docs/trips.md, load state (T12): the session loads until its first simulation.started (1); the job (2) is configured while running, so trip@2 opens with no cause interval and `unknown` completeness (T4: trip@<eventSeq of the job configuration>), with no truck or trailer reference and the unknown game mode. Without a loss it would close complete at its delivery (T13).
docs/trips.md, Attribution (T14): each toll 3-255 inside the active trip's window is attributed `trip` (the job has no available cargoLoaded, so never trip-before-loaded).

docs/trips.md, transitions 'any open | gap with a new suffix' (T10) and trip-reducer case 8: the gap [256] closes trip@2 {none, gap, partial} at the session's last label, the toll 255 (1,800,000,000,030; a gap carries no UTC, T15), with an event-loss interval (queueCount is not a consumer absence; trip-reducer T10 table) on the trip: its new suffix [256, 256], the record's lost times as monotonic bounds on the capture clock, and detail {cause: gap, the six counters, the record's range, redelivered: false} (Interval detail keys). The job becomes untracked. The gaps [257]-[260] find the slot idle: each is a session-level event-loss interval of its own suffix ('idle | gap with a new suffix').

Connection 2 (caller contract, Connections): `disconnected` then `session` at coverage 260; no trip is open, so no not-connected interval. The redelivered 1-255 are storage duplicates at or below the processed point (T5); the merged gap [256, 260] lies wholly inside coverage, so storage answers `covered` and nothing is stored or applied again (docs/storage.md, Coverage). job.delivered (261) has no open trip: whether the job is still untracked (the outcome of an untracked job) or the job-less checkpoint cleared it (an outcome with no attachable trip), it is attributed `ambiguous` and closes nothing (T14). The clear (262) adds nothing.
Attributions use one hand-written abbreviation: an entry with `eventSeqRange` [first, last] stands for one attribution per eventSeq in that range, in order; the test expands it before comparing.

Counts: 262 first commits (255 events and 5 gaps on connection 1, 261 and 262 on connection 2), 255 duplicates and 1 covered gap. Losses (G6, counted once from what storage committed as new rows): lostEvents 5 (one per delta gap), eventLoss 5; the covered redelivery counts nothing.
